knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral Expression For the Arc Length of a Parametric Curve Containing Special Functions

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=3 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,y=12 t + \cos{\left(t \right)}$
from $t=-1$ to $t=1$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2}\,\mathrm{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(12 t + \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)=12 - \sin{\left(t \right)}.
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L&=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)^2+\left(12 - \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)^2}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{9\sin^2(t)+144-24\sin(t)+\sin^2(t)}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{10 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 24 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 144}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
